2027-03-01.title: Monday of the fourth week of the Great Fast
readings: Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech's house
May the Lord of peace give you peace at all times
Jesus walks on the sea; Peter cries, “Lord, save me!”
2027-03-01.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fourth week. The Great Fast passes its middle this week; Mid-Fast is kept on Wednesday.
2027-03-01.verse: Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.
theo: The first reading finishes the story of Abraham in Gerar. Abimelech, warned by God in a dream, rises early and confronts Abraham: “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought such great guilt on me and my kingdom?” Abraham's answer is honest about his fear: “I did it because I thought, There is no fear of God at all in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.” He had judged a whole people without knowing them, and he was wrong: the pagan king turned out to fear God more than Abraham expected. Abimelech returns Sarah, gives gifts, and opens his land: “My land is before you; settle where it pleases you.” Then comes the turning point: “Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech, and also healed his wife and female slaves.” The man who caused the harm becomes the one who prays for healing. Here is a Lenten pattern: we acknowledge the wrong we have done, and then we pray, sincerely, for the very people we have wronged.

In the Gospel, fear meets Jesus on the water. The disciples are battling the wind through the night, and when they see Jesus walking toward them on the sea they cry out, “It is a ghost!” He answers at once: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.” Peter steps out, walks, and then looks at the wind instead of the Lord: “beginning to sink, he cried out, ‘Lord, save me!’ Jesus immediately reached out his hand and caught him.” St Augustine said that Peter sank because he trusted in himself, and rose because he cried out to the Lord; in himself he was weak, in Christ he was strong (in substance). Halfway through the Fast, many of us feel the wind more than at the beginning. The prayer of Peter is short enough for any moment: Lord, save me. And Paul's blessing is the answer to it: “Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with all of you.”
outline: Ask: when did fear make you misjudge a person or a situation?
The one who caused harm prays for healing.
Point 2 · Take heart, it is I
Jesus comes to us in the storm.
The hand that catches Peter; the Lord of peace.
“Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Pray for the one you wronged (Genesis 20:17)
Think of one person you have hurt or misjudged, and pray for him or her by name every day this week.
Each time fear or temptation rises today, say slowly: Lord, save me.
2027-03-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to your disciples walking on the sea, and you said to them: take heart, it is I; do not be afraid. When we judge others out of fear, correct us; when we have hurt others, teach us to pray for them as Abraham prayed for Abimelech. When the wind is strong and we begin to sink, stretch out your hand and catch us. Lord of peace, give us your peace at all times and in all ways, in this Great Fast and always. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the same Lord who said “it is I” comes to us, truly present, and the priest's blessing “peace be with you all” echoes Paul's prayer for the Lord of peace.

quick: Abraham, who wronged Abimelech out of fear, prayed for him, and God healed his house.
Paul prays that the Lord of peace will give peace at all times and in all ways.
Jesus walks on the sea, calls Peter, and catches him when he begins to sink.
2027-03-01.action: Pray today for someone you have wronged or misjudged.
2027-03-01.question: Where am I looking at the wind instead of at Jesus?

family.explain: The disciples were in a boat in a big storm at night. Jesus came to them walking on the water and said: be brave, it is me, do not be afraid. Peter walked on the water too, but when he looked at the waves he got scared and started to sink. He shouted: Lord, save me! And Jesus held his hand at once.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is afraid tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes us afraid, and how can we say ‘Lord, save me’ together?”

illus: A fisherman from Vizhinjam remembers the night his small boat lost its engine far from the shore. The swell was high and the radio was dead. His younger brother began to panic and wanted to jump and swim. The older man held him by the shirt and said: look at the lighthouse, only at the lighthouse, not at the waves. They rowed through the night with their eyes on that one turning light. At dawn a bigger boat found them. He says: the waves never stopped; I just stopped looking at them.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come to us in every storm. Take away our fear and give us your peace. Amen.
share: Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech (Genesis 20:17). Whom have I wronged, and have I prayed for them?
May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways (2 Thessalonians 3:16). Where do I most need God's peace?
Lord, save me! (Matthew 14:30). When did I last cry out to Jesus like Peter?
pm.resp: Lord, save us; give us your peace.
interc: For all who are afraid, especially the sick and those who live alone.
For fishermen and all who work at sea, especially on the coasts of Kerala.
For those we have hurt or misjudged, and for reconciliation in families.
For all who feel the Great Fast becoming heavy at its midpoint.
For peace in our country and in the world.
pm.close: Father, your Son walked on the waters and caught Peter as he sank. Give us faith to step out at his word, humility to pray for those we have wronged, and the peace that comes only from him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Abraham had wronged King Abimelech out of fear. He said: I thought, there is no fear of God at all in this place (Genesis 20:11). But the king was more honest than Abraham expected.
What does Abraham do then? He prays for the man he wronged: Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech (Genesis 20:17). This is a good Lenten practice: to pray for those we have hurt.

In the Gospel the disciples are in the storm, and Jesus comes walking on the sea: take heart, it is I; do not be afraid (Matthew 14:27). Peter walks to him, but when he notices the strong wind he begins to sink and cries out: Lord, save me! Jesus immediately reached out his hand and caught him (Matthew 14:30–31).

We are in the middle of the Great Fast. If you feel the wind more than before, look at Jesus, not at the waves, and say Peter's prayer. May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways (2 Thessalonians 3:16). Amen.
kids: Children, Peter walked on the water to Jesus! But when he looked at the big waves he got scared and started to sink. He shouted: Lord, save me! And Jesus caught his hand at once. When you are scared, you can say the same short prayer: Jesus, save me. He always hears.

intro: Theme: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
At the middle of the Fast: Abraham prays for the man he wronged, Jesus comes through the storm, and Peter learns to cry out.

points.h: Praying for the one we wronged
q: And the Lord restored the fortunes of Job when he had prayed for his friends; and the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Pray by name each day this week for one person you have wronged.

sub: The Lord with all of you.
q: The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the Lord lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Before sleep tonight, bless each member of your family with the words of Numbers 6.

q: Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to my neck.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Make “Lord, save me” your prayer in every moment of fear or temptation this week.

concl: Fear makes us misjudge others and sink in the storm; Jesus says, it is I.
The one who cries out to him is caught by his hand.
2027-03-01.resolve: For the rest of the Fast, keep your eyes on Jesus and pray for those you have hurt.
